Strange caterpillars and their final forms
The saturniidae and wattle cup caterpillars are amazing.
That right there tells you life on another planet would be utterly alien to us. I mean, look at life on our own planet and how different from us it is in pretty much every way.

It makes me wonder, what is the evolutionary purpose (or vestige) of being so beautifully ornate when they're in their more vulnerable form? It would seem more advantageous to blend in a bit more when they can only crawl and then become colorful when they are going to reproduce and can fly away from danger.

It's likely aposematism, or warning coloration. If a predator tries to eat one of those caterpillars, it'll be turned off because the caterpillar is spiky or poisonous. From then on, the predator remembers that there's no use in pursuing that type of prey.

Non-dangerous prey has also evolved warning coloration to mimic truly dangerous species, and it does help ward off predators. Hoverflies are good examples of this.
